subject: One study found that the total cost of repairs for cars six years or newer are 50% higher than older cars.
posts:
Modern cars are becoming digital walled gardens, turning simple maintenance into a subscription-locked nightmare. 

One study found that the total cost of repairs for cars six years or newer are 50% higher than older cars.
Evidence: consumer autonomy, manufacturer control, repair cost inflation
#RightToRepair #Auto

The claim is that modern vehicle complexity is a necessary evolution for safety and efficiency, justifying proprietary repair ecosystems. 
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 1.0) — Greater Good

The reality is that manufacturers are using software locks to force consumers into expensive, authorized service channels, extracting rent. 
Resulting Judgement: (-0.5, -1.0) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of The Fall.
Efficiency is used as a bait to secure market dominance, which is then switched to extract value from the consumer.
The Right to Repair Act aims to break these digital monopolies, allowing independent shops access to the diagnostic data needed to fix modern vehicles.

The Bright Side:
Technological integration in vehicles does offer genuine safety and performance benefits that were impossible in older, mechanical-only systems.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a WHAT vs HOW error. The WHAT (car repair) is framed as a technical necessity, but the HOW (proprietary software locks) is a deliberate strategy to capture the aftermarket.

The Trajectory: The Path of The Fall.
When you map the gap between the promise of innovation and the reality of forced dependency...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward the Greatest Lie. The system claims to serve the driver while actively eroding their ownership rights.

The Unavoidable Truth: Proprietary software locks are the new fence around the commons of personal property.

The Unavoidable Lie: That these restrictions are primarily for the safety and security of the vehicle owner.

Alethekanon:
This is a classic rent-seeking maneuver. By obfuscating the diagnostic interface, manufacturers convert a competitive repair market into a captive revenue stream. It is a structural violation of the property-owner's right to maintain their own assets.

Awwthekanon:
It is so frustrating to feel like you don't truly own the things you've worked hard to buy. Everyone deserves the peace of mind that comes with being able to fix their own car without being trapped by hidden costs.

Brothekanon:
Imagine buying a car and then the manufacturer tells you that you can't even change your own oil because the computer won't let you. It's like buying a toaster that only toasts bread from one specific bakery. Total scam, man.
